title: Healthcraft QBR: two-track deck templates & renewal pulse playbook
body:
Purpose:
This working doc contains two slide-deck templates (Standard and Enterprise) plus a lightweight renewal pulse tracker and a step-by-step playbook for running Quarterly Business Reviews. Built for CS Managers who run mixed portfolios (self-serve + enterprise), the goal is to standardize cadence while letting teams customize the story for each customer.

High-level guidance (use cases):
- Standard deck: fast 25–40 minute cadence for growth and mid-market accounts (adoption focus, tactical health, recommended outcomes).
- Enterprise deck: 45–75 minute cadence for strategic and renewal- at-risk accounts (executive narrative, risk matrix, financial impact, next-phase plan).
- Use the Renewal Pulse tracker before the QBR to decide whether the conversation is discovery-oriented (early renewal) or negotiation-oriented (at-risk).

Quick checklist (pre-meeting):
- Run Renewal Pulse (see tracker section) and tag risk tier: Green/Yellow/Red.
- Pull token & spend trends for last 90 days, top 3 slow endpoints, top 3 successful routes.
- Ask Solution Eng to prepare 1 slide if there are integration fixes or performance wins.
- Confirm exec attendance for Enterprise if renewal in next 90 days or tier=Red.
- Pre-send 3 agenda bullets and 2 data asks (usage snapshot, top P0s) 5 days before.

Standard Deck (10 slides, ~30 min):
1) Title + objective (1 slide) — 2 min: Meeting goal, participants, desired outcome (e.g., alignment to renewal + 3 next steps).
2) Highlights & wins (1 slide) — 5 min: Top 3 product wins, feature adoption, time-to-value anecdotes. Speaker note: call out customer quotes or support ticket that was closed.
3) Usage snapshot (2 slides) — 5 min: Tokens/embeddings/requests trend, peak latencies by route, percent cached. Visual: small charts.
4) Health signals (1 slide) — 4 min: Adoption metrics, latency SLA attainment, error rate trend. Call out any regressions.
5) Business outcomes (1 slide) — 4 min: Feature-to-business mapping (e.g., reduced support deflection by X%).
6) Risks & open blockers (1 slide) — 4 min: Top 3 risks, owners, ETA.
7) Roadmap fit / requested features (1 slide) — 3 min: What to expect next quarter, ask for prioritization.
8) Renewal/Next steps (1 slide) — 3 min: Recommended renewal path, potential discounts, decision timeline.
9) Action items & owners (1 slide) — 2 min: Clear list with who/when.
10) Appendix pointers (1 slide) — 1 min: Links to deeper metrics, support tickets, perf traces.

Speaker guidance: be outcome-first on slide 2 and 5. Keep technical detail in Appendix; surface only the customer impact in main flow.

Enterprise Deck (15 slides, ~60 min):
1) Executive summary & ask (1 slide) — 3 min: State the explicit renewal ask or strategic ask.
2) Customer goal alignment (1 slide) — 5 min: Reiterate business goals and KPIs the customer cares about.
3) Adoption & value map (2 slides) — 7 min: Mapping features to outcomes, ROI estimates, case studies inside account.
4) Usage & performance deep-dive (3 slides) — 10 min: Detailed charts, percentile latencies, KV cache hit rates, tail latency analysis.
5) Quality & regression monitoring (1 slide) — 5 min: Eval sets, hallucination/regression alerts, quality SLAs.
6) Cost & efficiency (1 slide) — 5 min: Per-token economics, recommended quantization/batching levers and projected savings.
7) Risk matrix (1 slide) — 6 min: Likelihood vs impact for top 6 risks; mitigations & fallback policies.
8) Operational readiness (1 slide) — 5 min: On-call playbooks, SLO attainment, runbook gaps.
9) Contract & renewal timeline (1 slide) — 5 min: Proposed commercial terms, decision checkpoints.
10) Success plan + milestones (1 slide) — 6 min: 90/180/365 day plan with deliverables and owners.
11) Appendix & supporting artifacts (2 slides) — remaining time: deep links to eval snapshots, perf traces, tickets.

Enterprise speaker notes: send pre-reads 72 hrs before. Include one page CFO-friendly ROI table. Always have closed-loop items with named exec owner.

Renewal Pulse Tracker (lightweight — use before scheduling):
- Fields to collect (pre-call): Renewal window, current ARR (string), last price, usage trend 30/90/180, top three value metrics, outstanding tickets >P2, exec sponsors identified, next contract decision date, estimated renewal probability (quantify).
- Triage heuristic:
  - Green: usage steady/increasing, no P1s, exec sponsor present -> standard deck, 25–40 min, no discount by default.
  - Yellow: usage dipping or >2 P2s, missing sponsor -> Standard+SE slide, invite AM+SE, consider retention pilot incentive.
  - Red: large usage drop, P1 or exec escalation, renewal <90 days -> Enterprise deck, urgent renewal plan, sales+legal loop.

Sample email invite (templates):
- Standard invite (short): “Agenda: 1) wins 2) health snapshot 3) next steps. Goal: align on success metrics for next quarter. Please share any data you want covered.”
- Enterprise invite (exec): include CFO/CTO summary paragraph and attach ROI 1-pager. Request 72-hr pre-read.

Playbook (step-by-step):
T-10 days: run Renewal Pulse, gather metrics, request pre-reads from SE and AM.
T-7 days: send invite and pre-read (Standard) or 72-hr pre-read (Enterprise). Confirm execs.
T-3 days: rehearsal with SE and AM, finalize appendix charts.
D-day: 1x facilitator (AM/CSM), 1x technical owner (SE), 1x note-taker. Timebox slides strictly.
D+2 days: send updated slides and action tracker.
D+7 days: 1:1 with exec sponsor for Enterprise to confirm next steps.

Action tracker template (text-friendly):
- Action: [short description] | Owner: [name] | Due: [YYYY-MM-DD] | Status: [open/in progress/closed] | Notes: [1–2 lines]

Risk signals (quick list to call out):
- Sustained drop in hourly throughput or user sessions.
- Increase in error rates > 2x baseline.
- Feature adoption stagnation despite enablement.
- Exec churn or reorg announced.
- Procurement/Legal delays beyond decision window.

Open questions / decisions we need help with:
- Do we standardize on a single renewal probability scoring system? (proposal: 0.0–1.0 with tags: outreach, negotiate, escalate)
- Is a 1-page CFO ROI mandatory for any renewal > $250k?
- What discount guardrails should CS own vs Sales (floor, approvals)?

Appendix (links & artifacts to attach to any deck):
- 90/180/365 usage CSV, 14-day tail-latency trace, top 10 support tickets export, security questionnaire status, commercial summary.

Notes to self / team TODOs (working):
- Build a slide pack generator that pulls token counts + latency percentiles into slides automatically (owner: Eng-Console; POC ticket created).
- Draft CFO ROI template and put into Confluence.
- Add a checkbox to Renewal Pulse for whether Dedicated/Private deployment is relevant.

References / prior examples:
- quick link to last enterprise QBR deck for Contoso (redacted) — see Confluence.
- internal postmortem: perf-regression-2024-11 (linked).

Version history:
- v0.1 2025-02-12 initial outline and two-track templates.
- v0.2 2025-02-25 added Enterprise risk matrix and Renewal Pulse heuristic.
- v0.3 2025-03-01 updated speaker notes and added playbook cadence.

If you want, I can also produce: a) a one-page CFO ROI template, b) a sample Standard and Enterprise deck in slides format, or c) a CSV Renewal Pulse template to drop into Google Sheets. Reply which you want next and I’ll add it under this folder.
